sources.claim: Whether a worker is an employee or an independent contractor depends on the actual working relationship (economic reality), not on the label in a contract; the federal rule has changed several times since 2021 and states may use stricter tests, so current federal and state rules must be checked.

sections.skill: Describe an employer's payroll duties in general terms

questions.prompt: What does withholding mean for an employer?

choices.text: Holding back the employee's whole paycheck as a penalty
Taking taxes out of pay and sending them to the agency

questions.correct_answer: Taking taxes out of pay and sending them to the agency
questions.intro: Hiring an EMPLOYEE brings PAYROLL duties. In general terms, an employer withholds certain taxes from the employee's pay, pays its own share of some payroll taxes, sends the money and reports to tax agencies on schedule, follows minimum wage and overtime rules, and gives the employee year-end tax forms. Many states also require registration and may require workers' compensation insurance. This course teaches the idea; rates, forms and deadlines vary. Many small businesses use a payroll service or an accountant.

sections.skill: A collection box at the counter

questions.prompt: The charity money belongs to whom?
questions.intro: Imagine a cashier who collects a small amount from each sale for a charity and must send it in every month. The money passes through the cashier but belongs to the charity. Withheld payroll taxes are similar: the employer holds them briefly and must send them on time. Spending them on rent is like spending the charity's money.
